claim: VemP allows Vibrio alginolyticus to adapt to changes in salinity by modulating expression of components of the protein targeting machinery.
source: One of the most recently discovered examples is the Vibrio export monitoring polypeptide (VemP) that allows Vibrio alginolyticus to adapt to changes in salinity by modulating expression of components of the protein targeting machinery (Ishii et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ishii et al., 2015

claim: V. alginolyticus is a Gram-negative marine-estuarine bacterium.
source: V. alginolyticus is a Gram-negative marine-estuarine bacterium that, unlike most bacteria, has two paralogs of SecDF (SecDF1 and SecDF2) to enhance protein export in cooperation with the SecYEG translocon.
evidence: Stated as established fact about the organism

claim: V. alginolyticus has two paralogs of SecDF (SecDF1 and SecDF2) to enhance protein export in cooperation with the SecYEG translocon.
source: V. alginolyticus is a Gram-negative marine-estuarine bacterium that, unlike most bacteria, has two paralogs of SecDF (SecDF1 and SecDF2) to enhance protein export in cooperation with the SecYEG translocon.
evidence: Stated as established fact about the organism

claim: In Na+-rich environments, V. alginolyticus utilizes the Na+-dependent SecDF1.
source: In Na+-rich environments, V. alginolyticus utilizes the Na+-dependent SecDF1; however, in Na+-limiting environments V. alginolyticus switches to the Na+-independent (presumably H+-dependent) SecDF2 (Ishii et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ishii et al., 2015

claim: In Na+-limiting environments V. alginolyticus switches to the Na+-independent (presumably H+-dependent) SecDF2.
source: In Na+-rich environments, V. alginolyticus utilizes the Na+-dependent SecDF1; however, in Na+-limiting environments V. alginolyticus switches to the Na+-independent (presumably H+-dependent) SecDF2 (Ishii et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ishii et al., 2015, with speculation about H+-dependence

claim: The switch between SecDF1 and SecDF2 is facilitated by the stalling activity of VemP.
source: The switch between SecDF1 and SecDF2 is facilitated by the stalling activity of VemP.
evidence: Stated as established mechanism based on prior work

claim: In Na+-rich environments, VemP is targeted by its signal sequence (SS) to the SecDF1-SecYEG translocon.
source: In Na+-rich environments, VemP is targeted by its signal sequence (SS) to the SecDF1-SecYEG translocon (Ishii et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ishii et al., 2015

claim: The force applied to VemP during protein translocation prevents VemP-dependent ribosome stalling.
source: The force applied to VemP during protein translocation prevents VemP-dependent ribosome stalling, thereby enabling the complete VemP to be translated and released from the ribosome.
evidence: Stated as established mechanism

claim: Under Na+-rich conditions, SecDF2 expression is repressed due to sequestration of the ribosome-binding site (RBS) of secDF2 within a stem-loop structure in the mRNA.
source: Under such conditions, SecDF2 expression is repressed due to sequestration of the ribosome-binding site (RBS) of secDF2 within a stem-loop structure in the mRNA (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by reference to Figure 1a showing the mechanism

claim: In Na+-limiting environments, VemP is not translocated due to the inactivity of SecDF1.
source: In Na+-limiting environments, however, VemP is not translocated due to the inactivity of SecDF1, and the resulting lack of force on the VemP nascent chain leads to ribosomal stalling (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by reference to Figure 1a

claim: The lack of force on the VemP nascent chain in Na+-limiting environments leads to ribosomal stalling.
source: In Na+-limiting environments, however, VemP is not translocated due to the inactivity of SecDF1, and the resulting lack of force on the VemP nascent chain leads to ribosomal stalling (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by reference to Figure 1a

claim: Ribosome stalling dissolves the stem-loop structure within the mRNA and exposes the RBS, thereby inducing expression of Na+-independent SecDF2.
source: Ribosome stalling dissolves the stem-loop structure within the mRNA, exposes the RBS and thereby induces expression of Na+-independent SecDF2 (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by reference to Figure 1a

claim: VemP-dependent stalling occurs when Q156 is in the P-site of the ribosome.
source: Biochemical studies have demonstrated that VemP-dependent stalling occurs when Q156 is in the P-site of the ribosome and that distinct amino acid residues within a 19aa window (138–156) of VemP are critical for efficient ribosome stalling (Figure 1a) (Ishii et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ishii et al., 2015 and reference to Figure 1a

claim: Distinct amino acid residues within a 19aa window (138–156) of VemP are critical for efficient ribosome stalling.

evidence: Supported by citation to Ishii et al., 2015 and reference to Figure 1a

claim: The VemP stalling sequence and force-sensing mechanism appears to be completely distinct from SecM and MifM.
source: Although VemP-mediated regulation of SecDF2 expression is reminiscent of other peptide-stalling regulatory systems (Ito and Chiba, 2013; Wilson et al., 2016), such as SecM (Nakatogawa and Ito, 2001) and MifM (Chiba et al., 2009), the VemP stalling sequence and force-sensing mechanism appears to be completely distinct (Ishii et al., 2015; Ito and Chiba, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: VemP 'short' carrying the 19 amino acid segment (138–156) produces mainly full-length LepB-VemP fusion protein with relatively little (10%) stalled peptide.

On the stalled ribosome, the upper α-helix of VemP encroaches directly upon the PTC and stabilizes an uninduced state of the PTC that prevents accommodation of the incoming A-tRNA and thereby promotes translation arrest (Figure 6a).
